jobs.title: Pharmacy Intern at Artes Rx
jobs.description: Employer: Artes Rx Expires: 10/30/2026 At ArtesRx, we are more than a pharmacy organization. We are a team of compassionate professionals dedicated to improving the lives of vulnerable patient populations through exceptional behavioral health and long-term care pharmacy services. As a leading organization in this space, ArtesRx brings together a growing network of pharmacies, expanding through strategic acquisitions while preserving the trusted local brands and relationships that have earned strong reputations in their communities. Together, we enhance medication access, adherence, and health outcomes for individuals who are often underserved due to the stigma surrounding mental illness and substance use disorders. Our mission is to empower our customers with pharmacy solutions tailored to their unique needs. By combining innovative technology with compassionate, high-touch service, we ensure efficient medication fulfillment and timely deliveries that foster trust, peace of mind, and healthier outcomes. We believe every individual deserves kindness, compassion, and dignity, and we know our success depends on honesty, integrity, and respect in every interaction. If you are passionate about helping others, thrive in a collaborative environment, and want your work to have a lasting impact, we invite you to explore a career with ArtesRx. Position Summary The Pharmacy Intern supports pharmacists in ensuring safe, effective, and compliant medication dispensing within a closed-door pharmacy setting. This position is intended for pharmacy students currently enrolled in an accredited PharmD program. Under direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist, the intern assists with order processing, medication preparation, clinical reviews, compliance tasks, and operational workflows in accordance with federal and state pharmacy regulations. Primary Responsibilities Assist with the maintenance of workflow, assigning pharmacy staff tasks required to maintain order and ensure an efficient and compliant pharmacy operation. Maintain a safe and clean working environment by complying with procedures, rules, and regulations outlined by the Board of Pharmacy, accreditation standards, and company policy. Stay current on pharmacological knowledge by studying existing and new legislation and keeping up to date with current continuing education. Perform other related duties as assigned. Assist health care providers and home agencies by answering questions and/or requests and taking verbal orders. Maintain effective communications with facilities to facilitate the fulfilment of patient care, foster enduring business relationships, and build customer loyalty. Perform job assignments in full compliance and complete understanding of URAC, state and federal laws and internal policies and procedures governing the handling, dispensing and distribution of medications dispensed by Parkview Health Services. Maintain a safe a clean working environment by complying with procedures, rules, and regulations outlined by the Board of Pharmacy, accreditation standards, and company policy. Read medication orders, decipher the prescription, input into the pharmacy system, and properly bill claims. Perform drug interaction checks on all prescriptions and contact the health care provider with any questions or concerns. Maintain records by recording and filing physicians' orders and prescriptions. Provide information and advice regarding drug interactions, side effects, dosage and proper medication use and disposal. Ability to work in a team environment to ensure the best possible patient care. Perform other related duties as assigned. Key Skills Consistent focus and attention to detail resulting in superior accuracy. Demonstrated organizational skills. Demonstrated ability to lift and move heavy packages (up to 30 lbs.) in compliance with safe handling procedures. Proficient computer skills and ability to easily navigate through pharmacy system and Microsoft Suite (Word, Excel, and Outlook) applications. Demonstrated ability to work independently on assigned tasks or in a team setting while focused on detail, accuracy, and productivity. Education/Experience Requirements Must be in the first or second professional year of an accredited pharmacy school Interns identified at P2 status or higher are required to hold a pharmacy intern permit that is active and is good standing in the state of New York Must be able to work one evening shift per week (until 10pm). Must work Friday evening (until 10pm) and Saturday (10am-3pm) on a rotating basis.

Professional development and networking opportunities within the health and safety industry.

Assists with instruction in putting, chipping, pitching, bunker play, full swing, course management, rules, etiquette, and pace of play. Prepares instructional areas, equipment, training aids, range balls, and other materials prior to programs and lessons. Assists with participant check-in, group organization, instructional stations, and program transitions. Provides basic instructional feedback to participants under the direction of professional golf staff. Assists with on-course instruction on the Par-3 and regulation golf courses. Helps create a positive, encouraging, safe, and welcoming learning environment for golfers of different ages, abilities, skill levels, and backgrounds. Assists with adaptive golf and other programs designed to make golf accessible to a broad range of participants. Assists staff in developing golf clinics, camps, leagues, lesson plans, instructional activities, and other player-development opportunities. Helps evaluate existing programs and identifies opportunities to improve the participant experience. Supports player-development efforts for juniors, beginners, women, seniors, and other developing golfers. Assists with utilizing the driving range, practice facilities, and Par-3 course as player-development resources. Assists with program registration, participation tracking, attendance, participant feedback, and program evaluation. Supports marketing and communication efforts related to golf programs and instructional opportunities. Maintains clean, organized, safe, and professional instructional and practice areas. Assists with golf shop and outside operations as assigned to gain a broader understanding of golf facility operations. Works with professional golf staff to establish internship learning goals and participates in ongoing coaching and feedback. May be given increasing responsibility for planning and delivering portions of clinics or instructional programs under the supervision of professional golf staff. Develops practical experience in golf instruction and coaching techniques, junior and adult programming, player development, customer service and hospitality, program management and evaluation, and public-sector golf operations. Performs other duties as assigned. SUPERVISORY DUTIES: This position does not have direct supervisory responsibilities. Interest in golf instruction, player development, golf operations, and the golf industry. Ability to effectively communicate with children, adults, guests, and coworkers. Strong customer service and interpersonal skills. Ability to create a positive and welcoming experience for program participants. Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team. Ability to follow direction and work within the scope of assigned responsibilities and training. Ability and willingness to learn, accept coaching and feedback, and demonstrate initiative.Ability to maintain a professional appearance and demeanor. Ability to prioritize participant, guest, and employee safety. Ability to organize equipment and instructional materials and assist with multiple activities and participant groups. Ability to work a flexible schedule that may include mornings, evenings, weekends, and holidays. Ability to consistently demonstrate the principles of the Indian Tree Way – Intentional Hospitality, Operational Excellence, and Making It Work. EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: Interest in golf instruction, PGA Golf Management, recreation, sports management, education, coaching, or a related field. Working knowledge of golf fundamentals, rules, and etiquette. Experience or demonstrated ability working effectively with children and adults. CPR/AED/First Aid certification or ability to obtain certification as required.Preferred Qualifications: Currently enrolled in or recently graduated from a PGA Golf Management, recreation, sports management, education, kinesiology, business, or related program. jobs.title: Outdoor Recreation Internships - Summer Camp at Camp Skylemar
jobs.description: Employer: Camp Skylemar Expires: 10/31/2026 Camp Skylemar seeks Outdoor Recreation Staff for this summer. Skylemar staff members are creative leaders and heroes while teaching and mentoring kids. Our mission is to make a positive impact in the world, one child at a time. Staff orientation week and weekly in-service training sessions provide a strong foundation to assume summer responsibilities. The state of Maine is more than a destination – it’s an experience that will take your breath away. In summer, there’s no better place to be than in Maine. From the beaches to the mountains, there’s so much to explore and enjoy during your free time. Counselors assist with team-building games and activities, spot kids as they navigate the obstacles on the low course, belaying kids on the high course and the climbing wall. Compensation packages start at $3,200. We also provide free housing, all meals, travel expenses, staff clothing, time off, WIFI, and laundry service. Skylemar provides and covers the costs of all specialized training. Positions run from June 13 – August 8, 2027. Some staff arrive earlier or stay later to fulfill their internship requirements. You can take a college class online while here. We provide free time to train/work out. We also have some simple ways Skylemar staff members can earn extra money this summer. We also offer staff the ability to work out, train, and take online classes. We offer internship credit. Most educational institutions require prior approval before the start of an internship. Check with your institution to be sure this opportunity meets any requirements.

jobs.title: Program Operations Intern - Civic Education at Cato Institute
jobs.description: Employer: Cato Institute Expires: 11/02/2026 To be considered for this role, you must apply directly through our online application. OverviewSphere Education Initiatives is a nonpartisan educator professional development program housed at the Cato Institute that provides teachers and administrators in grades 5–12 with viewpoint-diverse resources to strengthen free speech, civil discourse, and civic culture in their classrooms. Sphere's flagship program is Sphere Summit — a fully funded, five-day in-person event held twice each summer in Washington, DC — alongside Sphere on the Road (school and district visits), the Sphere Alumni Fellowship (a six-month program for Summit graduates), and an expanding library of curriculum resources, including lesson plans, toolkits, and multimedia content. The internship covers program operations, curriculum creation, and administrative duties. The workload is event-focused and logistically demanding during Summit season, shifting to content development and program support at other times. It is ideal for applicants interested in K–12 civics education and educator professional growth who are also dependable, organized, and comfortable with operational tasks — including inventory management, shipping coordination, and CRM maintenance — as well as more in-depth curriculum and program work.ResponsibilitiesAssist with the Sphere Summit application review and program development, including communicating with participants and handling logistical arrangements.Provide operational support for Sphere on the Road and other Sphere events, including preparing materials, shipping packages, and managing inventory using EZO.Maintain and update Sphere's educator contacts and program records in Salesforce, including list maintenance and record management.Develop curriculum resources for teachers of grades 5–12 that promote civil discussion, diverse viewpoints, and civic participation in the classroom.Assist with the Sphere Alumni Fellowship, including organizing events, conducting research, and managing program logistics.Assist in creating program materials, lookbooks, and other communications as assigned.Assist at Sphere Summit and other Cato events as needed, including participant support and on-site logistics.Required QualificationsStrong interest in K–12 civic education, civil discourse, and educator professional development; comfortable engaging respectfully and constructively with educators and participants from diverse viewpoints.Understanding of libertarian and classical-liberal thought and aligning with Cato's principles of individual liberty, limited government, free markets, and peace, while recognizing that Sphere's programs are explicitly nonpartisan and support educators across the political spectrum.Clear written and verbal communication; professional demeanor in participant-facing and vendor-facing interactions.Reliable follow-through in event-driven settings with changing priorities and strict logistics timelines.Professionalism, humility, and an entrepreneurial mindset — willingness to handle both substantive project work and operational responsibilities as needed.Professionalism, reliability, and attention to detail — this work requires accuracy in both data handling and written output, as well as consistent follow-through across operational and content tasks.Preferred QualificationsFamiliarity with Salesforce or a similar CRM for contact management, list hygiene, and basic reporting.Proficient in Microsoft Excel for list management and basic tracking.Prior experience in program administration, event coordination, or education-related work through a school, nonprofit, or civic organization.Knowledge of K–12 curriculum design or educational content development.The Cato Internship ProgramCato’s paid internships are available for undergraduates, recent graduates, graduate students, law students, and early-career professionals who are strongly committed to individual liberty, limited government, free markets, and peace—principles that together form libertarianism, also known as “classical liberalism,” “market liberalism,” or, to many of our international friends, simply “liberalism.” All Cato interns participate in the same intensive seminar series, which covers a wide range of topics in history, philosophy, policy, and professional development. Interns also assist with events and occasionally support Cato staff with other daily tasks. Interns receive competitive pay. Part-time roles are adjusted accordingly and require a minimum of 25 hours per week. Program participants must be able to attend in person in Washington, DC.For more information about the internship program and experience, we encourage you to explore our website. If you have any questions, email studentprograms@cato.org.

jobs.description: Employer: Clean Harbors Expires: 11/08/2026 Clean Harbors Deer Park Incinerator is seeking a Electrical Engineer Intern to join our safety-focused team. This internship provides students with the opportunity to gain hands-on experience while supporting real projects that contribute to business priorities across our environmental, energy, and industrial services operations. We are searching for a reliable and team-oriented individual with an excellent commitment to safety to join our growing team during Summer 2027!This internship is an in-person opportunity based at our Deer Park, TX Incinerator and is not eligible for remote work. Interns will work alongside experienced professionals, gain exposure to our industry, and develop practical skills that support their academic and early career goals.Start dates for our Summer 2027 Internship Program are May 17th or May 24th of 2027. Internships will run through the summer and end in August.Why Intern with Clean Harbors? Health and Safety is our #1 priority and we live it 3-6-5!Competitive payClean Harbors offers students the opportunity to gain hands-on experience while working alongside professionals who are leading the way in environmental, energy, and industrial services.Our internship program is designed to provide: Engagement with teams, mentors, and leaders across the organization;Experience through meaningful projects that support real business priorities;Education about the environmental services industry and Clean Harbors' operations;Exposure to different career paths across our lines of business.Key Responsibilities Ensuring that Health and Safety is the number one priority by complying with all safe work practices, policies, and processes and acting in a safe manner at all times;Assist in the implementation and maintenance of the Mechanical Integrity ProgramLearn about corrosion mechanisms and participate in corrosion monitoring and mitigation activitiesGain exposure to Process Safety Management (PSM) principles, including the Process Hazard Analysis (PHA) process, Management of Change (MOCs), Operating Procedures, Incident Investigation, and other elements of PSMTake initiative and demonstrate a proactive approach to learning and problem-solvingAdhere to safety protocols and ensure compliance with industry standards and regulations, including the pillars of Process Safety Management (PSM)What does it take to intern with Clean Harbors? Currently pursuing a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering at an accredited college or university;Strong interest in learning about the environmental services industry;Ability to work collaboratively in a professional team environment;Strong communication, organization, and problem-solving skills;Proficiency in Microsoft Office or other relevant technical tools;Proficiency in CAD or similar software for updating and modifying engineering drawings;Knowledge of P&IDs and piping ISOs preferred;Lift to 50lbs, climb ladders, stoop, bend, stand for prolonged periods, exposed to various weather conditions and work at heightsWant to learn more about starting your career with Clean Harbors?As a Clean Harbors intern, you will gain hands-on experience working alongside field teams and operational leaders who support environmental and industrial services across North America. jobs.title: AmeriCorps Summer Teaching Fellow at SSC Learning Network
jobs.description: Employer: SSC Learning Network Expires: 11/08/2026 About Breakthrough Silicon ValleyBreakthrough Silicon Valley launches talented students who have been historically excluded from higher education on the path to college, and inspires high school and college students to become the next generation of leaders, advocates, and educators. BTSV’s six -year college access and success program, which supports students from 7th grade to first year of college, has proven to be effective in preparing these students for college: a stunning 99% of BTSV graduates attend college immediately after high school. BTSV’s tuition-free program provides year-round out-of-school time academic support, advising, and advocacy for a diverse group of talented students, most of whom come from under-resourced communities and will be the first generation in their family to go to college. Through our students-teaching-students model, BTSV also provides a consummate professional development experience providing talented high school and college students the opportunity to understand the K-12 system and the drivers of educational inequities, and to design and teach classes under the direction of seasoned educators. Located in San Jose, California, Breakthrough Silicon Valley is an affiliate of The Breakthrough Collaborative, a leading national service organization that acts as the national voice for 25 Breakthrough sites across the country. About the Summer Teaching FellowshipYour Impact: Our summer program could not be what it is every year without the dedicated service of our Teaching Fellows. You won’t just be a teacher. You’ll be a mentor and a role model to your students. You will witness how your leadership helps your students grow personally and progress academically in just a few weeks. What does a typical summer look like?Pre-Service Orientation TrainingYour journey begins with an immersive Pre-Service Orientation. During the first few days, you'll dive into the essentials of lesson planning, instructional strategies, and classroom management techniques. Alongside other AmeriCorps Teaching Fellows, you’ll build connections, form lasting friendships, and become familiar with Breakthrough's vibrant culture and mission. During this time, you’ll meet your Instructional Coach, a seasoned educator in your subject area, who will mentor you throughout the summer. This guidance will set the foundation for your success in the classroom.The Summer Program ExperienceTeaching Fellows are responsible for delivering engaging instruction in core academic subjects such as reading, writing, math, and science, as well as leading elective classes that inspire and motivate middle school students. In addition, Fellows serve as Crew Leaders, fostering community and building relationships through daily crew time by planning and facilitating icebreakers, energizers, and team-building activities. Fellows serve closely with an Instructional Coach, participating in regular meetings to strengthen their teaching and leadership skills while incorporating feedback to support continuous professional growth as educators.But it's not all work! Breakthrough’s summer is packed with joy-filled traditions like college campus visits, the summer talent show, Spirit Week, field days, and the Breakthrough Olympics. You’ll not only help students learn but also build a community of fun, encouragement, and support that will leave a lasting impact.Wrap-Up Week and Reflecting on Your ImpactAt the end of the summer, you'll celebrate the achievements of your students and reflect on the incredible growth you’ve witnessed in them—and yourself. Wrap-Up Week provides time to document these experiences and share your insights. It also offers career-building opportunities through panels featuring local professionals in fields like counseling, educational technology, higher education, and youth development. These sessions will help you envision your next steps as a future leader in education or beyond.This journey will not only give you hands-on teaching experience but also prepare you for a meaningful career, surrounded by a community that celebrates growth, learning, and the joy of teaching. Mentorship and GuidanceYou will serve under the mentorship of an experienced Instructional Coach, who will review your lesson plans, provide daily feedback, and train you in effective teaching strategies, classroom management, and student assessment techniques. Teaching Fellows will receive their Performance Review at the conclusion of their service. jobs.title: Health Informatics Intern at EMI Advisors LLC
jobs.description: Employer: EMI Advisors LLC Expires: 11/15/2026 *This internship is only available in or around the following cities:-Cleveland, Ohio-Cincinnati, Ohio-San Juan, PREMI Advisors LLC (EMI Advisors) is a digital transformation firm that harnesses disruptive solutions for the greater good. Our team works side-by-side with our clients and partners to help them make sense of messy and disconnected policy, program, business, and technical requirements and turn them into systems that work together. We are mission-driven and love working with smart, diverse, and passionate people every day. We consider it a privilege to design and build solutions that improve the health and well-being of individuals, communities, societies, and our planet. EMI Advisors values candidates with a growth mindset: believing your talents can be developed through hard work, smart strategies, and input from others. About the Role As the Health Informatics Intern, you will help us research how government agencies and organizations are adopting health data standards, map how different data systems and care delivery programs connect, and support the data gathering and visualization that helps our clients make better decisions while gaining hands-on experience in a consulting environment. You will report to our Health practice leadership team and work alongside project managers, data analysts, and subject matter experts. Key Responsibilities Research how government agencies and organizations are adopting health data standards and help summarize what you find for the project team. Support environmental scans and landscape analyses that map how different data systems, programs, and stakeholders connect. Help gather, clean, and organize data to support data visualization and reporting. Review policy, program, and market information, and translate it into clear summaries. Help prepare client deliverables, including reports, presentations, environmental scans, and technical assistance materials. Support project coordination, including scheduling, meeting notes, task tracking, and file organization. Participate in internal and client meetings and communicate progress and follow-up items clearly. Contribute to special projects or firm-wide initiatives as needed. Qualifications Currently pursuing, or recently completed, a master's degree in health informatics, health policy, healthcare administration, or a related field. Genuine interest in health informatics, health data standards, interoperability, or health and human services technology work, including staying current with the field on your own rather than only when it’s assigned. Relevant coursework, research, volunteer work, internship experience, or project experience in health informatics, data, or technology. Strong research, analytical, writing, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to synthesize information and communicate findings clearly, in writing and out loud. Strong organization, time management, and attention to detail. Working familiarity with Microsoft 365 tools, including PowerPoint, Word, Excel, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams. Familiarity with cloud-based collaboration tools such as Google Drive is a plus. Ability to learn new topics and tools quickly, and to work both independently and as part of a team. Familiarity with health data standards such as HL7â FHIRâ, and coded terminologies like LOINCâ, SNOMED-CTâ, and ICD-10, is a plus but not required. No prior professional work experience is required. Other Job Requirements Authorized to work in the United States. A quiet and stable environment to make and receive calls and other communications. Ability to travel by car, train, or plane if needed for client meetings or firm events; anticipated to be less than 10% of the internship.

jobs.title: Invasive Plant Member at American Conservation Experience
jobs.description: Employer: American Conservation Experience Expires: 11/15/2026 SummaryAmerican Conservation Experience, a nonprofit Conservation Corps, in partnership with San Antonio Missions National Historical Park is seeking one member to contribute to Invasive Species removal projects alongside The National Park Service (NPS) Staff.For more information about ACE, please visit our website.Start Date: January 2027Estimated End Date: Late July/early August 2027 (dependent on start date)*a 29-week minimum commitment is required *Location Details/Description: San Antonio Missions National Historical Park, San Antonio, TXSan Antonio Missions National Historical Park protects, preserves, restores, and interprets four Spanish Colonial missions and their associated cultural landscape features along the upper San Antonio River. The park consists of approximately 1,000 acres of land and contains numerous cultural resource sites which clearly illustrate the life and legacy of the 18th Century Spanish frontier in Texas. The park combines urban and rural settings and cultural and natural resources and offers outdoor recreational activities like hiking, biking, and picnicking.All five missions in San Antonio, Texas, including Mission Valero (the Alamo) are a single UNESCO World Heritage Site, the San Antonio Missions World Heritage Site. Four of the five (Mission Concepción, Mission San José, Mission San Juan, and Mission Espada) comprise San Antonio Missions National Historical Park. Together they are the most complete and intact group of Spanish Colonial mission complexes in the world. Through these mission communities, the Spanish asserted political, religious, and cultural influence on its newly claimed territories. With labor recruited from Indigenous South communities, the Spanish built these missions on the northern frontier of New Spain. All four missions within the park are active parishes and part of San Antonio.For more information about San Antonio Missions National Historical Park, please visit the NPS website.Position Overview:The purpose of this internship is to expose the ACE member to natural resource management practices at an urban unit of the National Park Service (NPS). The primary emphasis of their work will focus on riparian habitat restoration, utilizing herbicide treatments and the physical removal of exotic plant species. The members will spend a portion of their time assisting the Integrated Resources Division Staff with developing plans and methods for the eradication and removal of various exotic plant species. This will include reviewing and analyzing the findings of the exotic botanical survey report, defining areas of high priority, and developing operating procedures for the chemical or physical removal of each exotic species discovered. This will also entail researching aquatic herbicides in coordination with the Park Biologist and setting up test plots to assess the efficacy of different herbicides in removing invasive species from a historically significant waterway.The member will also assist the resource team in targeted herbicide treatments in areas of high natural resource sensitivity. The member will assist with the development of a geospatial data collection operating procedure for collecting metadata regarding the locations of invasive species. They will also continue surveying sections of the park and recording locations of invasive species. During targeted treatments, the member will be tasked with mapping and documenting treatment efforts for future planning. This information will be used for Government Performance and Results Act (GPRA) reporting and documentation in support of regional Invasive Plant Management Team efforts. A portion of the member’s time will also be spent documenting their experience and developing outreach and education materials related to the importance of riparian ecosystems and the value of invasive plant treatments within the broader field of natural resource management. This portion of the internship could include drafting social media posts for the park’s accounts, assisting with the development of natural resource content for the park website, and participating in a park outreach event.Additionally, the member will be expected to assist with high-priority park operations as they arise. For example, the park often hosts large-scale events that require support from the natural resource program, such as integrated pest management actions.This individual placement is meant to facilitate professional development and promote exposure to land management agencies and networking with professionals. This could include gaining experience in different conservation fields and shadowing different work groups.Schedule: Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The member can expect to spend approximately 60% of their time on office work and 40% on field work.Position BenefitsLiving Allowance: The ACE Member is expected to contribute ~40 hours/week and will receive a living allowance of $1000/week to offset the costs of food and incidental expenses, dispersed bi-weekly.This position is part of the Public Land Corps Hiring Authority: Members serving under this agreement must meet the PLC Eligibility Requirements to be considered for this position. Members may be eligible for a federal hiring authority upon completion of their term of service and 640 hours of service. If the duration of a PLC-eligible term is not long enough for Members to accrue 640 hours of service (~16 weeks), the total hours served at the completion of the term may be eligible to be combined with hours accrued from another PLC-eligible term to meet the 640 hours requirement. PLC projects also include specific eligibility requirements such as age (You must be between the ages of 16 and 30. Some agencies also interpret these guidelines to include veterans up to age 35) and citizenship. Please contact ACE staff with questions about eligibility, or view general eligibility information on our website.Housing: Housing is the responsibility of the member and not provided by ACE or NPS. There are numerous affordable rental options in the San Antonio metro area. Provided Training/Orientation: ACE members will receive position specific training and an orientation outlining ACE policies and procedures, clear guidance on prohibited activities, and networks for support. Specific training in herbicide usage will be provided.Qualifications Required:Members must be authorized to work in the United States. ACE does not provide sponsorship for employment visas. Willing and able to represent ACE and the partner organization in a professional, positive, and enthusiastic manner. Ability to be both self-directed/work alone, and be a positive, contributing member of a group.A valid driver's license and an insurable driving record (documentation to be provided upon request). Members must be 21+ to drive due to ACE’s insurance and liability requirements.Willing to undergo and must pass the required criminal history checks Ability to perform the essential duties of the position with or without reasonable accommodation.ACE Members will need to complete bi-weekly timesheets, beginning of term feedback forms, end of term evaluations and for longer terms, a mid-term evaluation. Member may not participate in any prohibited activities as listed in the Member Service Agreement.To learn more about eligibility requirements, please visit our website located on our Indeed homepage.Preferred:Competitive applicants for this position can hold or be pursuing a bachelor's degree and/or have relevant experience in subject areas such as Geographic Information Systems (GIS) (Geography, Cartography, or Geoscience), Natural Resources, Environmental Sciences, Biology, Botany, or other related fields. Some experience with GIS and spreadsheets/databases is preferred, specifically with regards to data editing, map generation and construction.Ability and willingness to work outdoors for extensive periods of time in multiple weather conditions, particularly high heat, carrying equipment in excess of 25 lbs (backpack sprayer).Deep interest in NPS, mapping software, and invasive species management.Physical Demands, Work Environment and Working Conditions: Physical Demands: Requires frequent sitting, standing, walking, carrying, using hands to handle or feel, reaching with hands and arms, talking and hearing. Manual dexterity required for use of various tools, computer keyboard/mouse and other office equipment. Required to stoop, kneel, climb stairs, and/or crouch.Vision Requirements: Requires close, distance, peripheral and depth perception vision as well as the ability to focus. Weight Lifted or Force Exerted: Frequently moves up to 25-40 lbs., ability to move up to 50 pounds.Environmental: Outdoor and indoor conditions. Work environment conditions can change frequently; working under adverse weather conditions and in various climates. Mainly indoor, office environment conditions; indoor air quality is good and temperature is controlled.Noise Environment: Moderate noise such as in a business office with equipment and light traffic.Travel: This position does not require unique travel. Environmental Conditions/Hazards: The ACE member(s) may encounter environmental conditions/hazards including extreme heat or cold, rocky terrain, swamp or wetland conditions, biting insects, and potentially dangerous wildlife. The member is expected to conduct duties in a safe and orderly manner so as not to endanger self, fellow staff/members or resources. Vehicle and Equipment Use/Safety: If a vehicle is required for the accomplishment of the duties, one will be provided by the NPS or ACE. Any tools required for the accomplishment of the duties will be provided by the NPS. Use of personal protective equipment (PPE), typically provided by the NPS, will be mandatory for any activity that requires it. Strict adherence to NPS and ACE equipment training, certification and safety protocols is required. To Apply: Please submit your resume, a cover letter demonstrating your interest and experience, and contact information for three professional/academic references to ACE’s online application page for this position on our website. Early consideration will be given as applications are received. This position may close at any time. If you have any questions regarding this position please feel free to contact Senior Member Manager, Sabrina Caruso.If you meet at least 70 percent of the qualifications, we want to hear from you!ACE participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information when you are enrolled in a program to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S.EEO: Employment or Service with ACE is based upon ability, qualifications, attitude, and job-related factors. Every qualified employee, member, or applicant has the same opportunity for recruitment, hire, training, transfer, promotion, compensation, demotion, termination, benefits, employee activities, and general treatment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, creed, national origin, pregnancy, ancestry, citizenship status, genetic information, veteran or military status, physical or mental disability, sexual orientation, medical condition, marital or parental status, political affiliation, ethnicity, hair texture or style, arrest record, caste, hereditary status, endogamy, or any other classification protected by applicable local, state, or federal law.

jobs.title: Sales and Recruiting Intern at ProCare Therapy
jobs.description: Employer: ProCare Therapy Expires: 11/15/2026 Start Date: May 24, 2027 End Date: July 23, 2027 About the Opportunity Launch your career with hands-on recruiting experience at ProCare Therapy, where we make life better for those who make lives better. Our summer internship is a production role focused on recruiting—finding and connecting qualified candidates with open jobs. You’ll work directly with territory leaders and an assigned territory, learning how to run a recruiting desk while contributing to real hiring needs. Your Soliant Launch Experience During the ProCare Therapy Launch Program, you will: Launch Your Career through real recruiting experience and professional development. Find Your People by building relationships with mentors, leaders, and teammates who are invested in your success. Write Your Story by gaining the skills, confidence, and experiences that shape your career. Make Life Better by connecting talented professionals with opportunities that positively impact healthcare, education, and pharmacy communities nationwide. What You’ll Do Partner with territory leaders to understand open positions and recruiting priorities. Source candidates through job boards, resume databases, outreach, and other recruiting tools. Contact prospective candidates to discuss opportunities, qualifications, interests, and availability. Support candidate screening and coordinate the next steps with your assigned team. Build and maintain a pipeline of candidates for current and upcoming openings. Keep candidate records and recruiting activity accurate and up to date. Work toward established activity and production goals with coaching from experienced recruiters and leaders. Participate in cohort training, team discussions, and feedback sessions. Training and Program Structure Week 1: Participate in classroom-style training to learn our business, recruiting process, systems, and expectations. Week 2: Continue classroom training while beginning to recruit in a structured, supported setting. Week 3 through the end of the program: Split your time between cohort learning and working alongside your assigned territory, taking on recruiting desk responsibilities with ongoing coaching. What We’re Looking For A college student interested in sales and a career centered on building relationships. Strong communication skills and a willingness to initiate conversations with new people. A goal-oriented mindset and motivation to contribute to team results. Coachability, curiosity, and the ability to apply feedback. Strong organization, follow-through, and attention to detail. Resilience and a positive approach to a fast-paced environment. Availability to participate throughout the internship dates. What You’ll Gain You’ll develop practical skills in candidate sourcing, outreach, screening, relationship building, and managing a recruiting pipeline. Through classroom learning and daily work with your territory, you’ll gain a clear understanding of how recruiting supports business results—and experience making a meaningful contribution to a team.

Internship Program RequirementsMust be available to work a variety of shifts, including mornings, afternoons, evenings, weekends, and holidays.This is a fully on-site internship at one of the designated Marriott Vacations Worldwide resort locations.Candidates must be actively pursuing a college degree at any level.While students majoring in Hospitality or Business Management are preferred, applicants from other academic disciplines are also encouraged to apply.A valid driver’s license may be required, depending on scope of role. Internship Resort Operations Position Descriptions Food & Beverage- Rotate through various food outlets based on property size and offerings (e.g., pool bar, marketplace, etc.)- Gain experience in both front and back of house operations- Learn key roles such as: Server, Food prep/Cook, Expeditor, Bar Staff- Observe and learn key components of inventory control, placing orders and handling alcohol responsibly.- Partnership with Recreation team for themed events, holidays, and property celebrations. Front Office- Learn and apply brand-standard welcoming techniques to deliver an exceptional guest experience- Welcome and assist guests and owners during the check-in and check-out process- Learn how to be a helpful resource to guests by taking care of requests and inquiries- Learn to handle daily front desk tasks and participate in problem solving- Learn the difference between ownership and nightly reservations- Observe and learn the pre-arrival process for guests- Get to know room locations and how they are assigned Recreation/Activities:- Promote fun resort activities and facilities to guests of all ages- Lead and support activities like trivia, pool games, outdoor fun, and educational programs- Help with setup and execution of special events such as food tastings and local storytelling- Understand the importance of interacting directly with guests to create fun and memorable experiences- Learn how to plan and organize daily and special activities- Observe and support areas like health and fitness, childcare, and team leadership Interns must be able to reach overhead and below knee level, and perform physical activities such as bending, twisting, pulling, and stooping. jobs.title: Sport Management Intern / Camp Counselor at Camp Lokanda
jobs.description: Employer: Camp Lokanda Expires: 11/16/2026 We welcome you to the ultimate summer internship and job experience! jobs.title: Medical Coding Intern at Quartz Health Solutions, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Quartz Health Solutions, Inc. Expires: 11/21/2026 Quartz is seeking a Medical Coding Intern to join our team from June through December 2027. This opportunity is ideal for a student pursuing a career in Medical Coding or Health Information Technology who is interested in applying classroom knowledge in a real-world healthcare environment. As a Medical Coding Intern, you will work alongside experienced coding professionals, contribute to meaningful projects, and gain valuable exposure to the health insurance industry. Throughout the internship, you will develop technical coding knowledge, professional skills, and industry experience that will support your future career goals. Internship Benefits: Competitive pay Networking and team-building opportunities Week-long intern retreat in Madison, Wisconsin (June 1-4, 2027) Personality and productivity workshops, including DiSC and Working Genius Dedicated intern buddy and mentorship support Mock interview and résumé development workshops Job shadowing opportunities Paid volunteer experience Access to Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) ResponsibilitiesWhat You'll Do As a Medical Coding Intern, you will gain hands-on experience while supporting key initiatives within the Coding Integrity Unit. Responsibilities may include: Assisting with coding logic denial reviews and analysis Researching CPT, ICD-10, and coding guideline updates Supporting the development, maintenance, and review of coding policies Conducting reviews of unlisted procedure codes Assisting with coding software administration and maintenance Participating in coding-related research projects Collaborating with coding professionals to support coding accuracy and regulatory compliance Analyzing coding trends and identifying opportunities for process improvement What You'll Learn Throughout the internship, you will develop knowledge and skills in areas such as: Medical Coding & Healthcare Knowledge Application of coding concepts to medical claims HIPAA regulations and compliance requirements Health insurance products and operations Industry regulations, trends, and market dynamics Professional Skills Problem-solving and analytical thinking Written and verbal communication Time management and organization Professional workplace etiquette and collaboration Technology & Business Tools Microsoft Excel Microsoft Outlook Microsoft Word Microsoft PowerPoint Coding software and systems used within the healthcare industry QualificationsTo be considered for this opportunity, candidates must: Demonstrated interest in Medical Coding as a possible career path Ability to work 20 hours per week from June to December 2027 Seeking a student pursuing a Medical Coding or Health Information Technology Diploma or Degree program and Graduating between May 2027 and May 2028 Completion of a CPT and ICD-10 Coding course by the start of internship Must live within a 3-hour radius of Madison, WI and be willing to travel to headquarters from June to August Attend the summer intern program kickoff and retreat (June 1-4, 2027), and final intern presentation (Late July/Early August) Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the United States without requiring work visa sponsorship from Quartz, now or in the future Hardware and equipment will be provided by the company, but candidates must have access to high-speed, non-satellite Internet to successfully work from home. We offer an excellent benefit and compensation package, opportunity for career advancement and a professional culture built on the foundations of Respect, Responsibility, Resourcefulness and Relationships. To support a safe work environment, all employment offers are contingent upon successful completion of a pre-employment criminal background check. Quartz values and embraces diversity and is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, status as a protected veteran, among other things, or status as a qualified person with disability.
